catalogue.description: This assembly illustrates Sentinel’s software detection pipeline. Its chip-like appearance is a visual metaphor for the research system.
catalogue.title: Sentinel core

catalogue.description: The glowing diamond gives the software’s prediction a visible focal point. Its light and movement are storytelling effects.
catalogue.title: Decision beacon

catalogue.description: The input stage maps feature sequences into the representation used by the model. Each sequence contains ten time steps.
catalogue.title: Input projection

catalogue.description: Convolution captures nearby changes within a feature sequence. This plate illustrates that stage of the Conformer architecture.
catalogue.title: Convolution

catalogue.description: Self-attention relates events across the sequence to provide temporal context. The separated plate makes that processing stage visible.
catalogue.title: Self-attention

catalogue.description: Two prediction heads produce a binary anomaly decision and a forensic attack classification. One visual plate represents both outputs.
catalogue.title: Prediction heads

catalogue.description: The rising bars illustrate gradient saliency: input features that influence a prediction. Their heights are illustrative; real attributions depend on the input.
catalogue.title: Feature influence
catalogue.visibility: This part appears in the explanation chapter.

catalogue.description: The record symbol illustrates the link between an alert, its explanation and the proposed response. The research prototype supports audit records for review.
catalogue.title: Audit record
catalogue.visibility: This part appears in the evidence chapter.

catalogue.description: This node represents network-traffic records from the TON_IoT research dataset. The portfolio shows an illustrated source, rather than a live network feed.
catalogue.title: Network traffic

catalogue.description: This node represents the Fridge sensor domain in TON_IoT. It is one of seven IoT sources illustrated around the core.
catalogue.title: Fridge sensor

catalogue.description: This node represents the GPS_Tracker domain in TON_IoT. Its movement in the scene is part of the visual story.
catalogue.title: GPS tracker

catalogue.description: This node represents the Garage_Door sensor domain in TON_IoT. The model places this source alongside other IoT telemetry.
catalogue.title: Garage door

catalogue.description: This node represents the Modbus domain in TON_IoT. The intrusion chapter highlights it in a simulated incident.
catalogue.title: Modbus telemetry

catalogue.description: This node represents the Motion_Light sensor domain in TON_IoT. It illustrates a separate source entering the shared analysis pipeline.
catalogue.title: Motion light

catalogue.description: This node represents the Thermostat sensor domain in TON_IoT. Its connecting path illustrates how sensor records reach the core.
catalogue.title: Thermostat

catalogue.description: This node represents the Weather sensor domain in TON_IoT. It completes the seven illustrated IoT sources.
catalogue.title: Weather sensor

catalogue.description: This node represents Linux_Disk host records in TON_IoT. Host activity adds another view alongside network and sensor data.
catalogue.title: Linux disk

catalogue.description: This node represents Linux_Memory host records in TON_IoT. It is one of five host domains included in the research pipeline.
catalogue.title: Linux memory

catalogue.description: This node represents Linux_Process host records in TON_IoT. It illustrates the process-activity source within the host group.
catalogue.title: Linux processes

catalogue.description: This node represents Windows_7 host records in TON_IoT. The label identifies a dataset domain used by the research prototype.
catalogue.title: Windows 7 host

catalogue.description: This node represents Windows_10 host records in TON_IoT. Together, the host nodes complete the thirteen illustrated telemetry domains.
catalogue.title: Windows 10 host

catalogue.description: The thin lines connect telemetry sources to the processing assembly. They illustrate data flow through the software pipeline.
catalogue.title: Signal paths

catalogue.description: The moving points help you follow signals toward the core. Their timing is animated for the story and does not show live packet traffic.
catalogue.title: Travelling signals

catalogue.description: The base visually supports the processing layers as the model transforms. It is a decorative part of this 3D teaching model.
catalogue.title: Core foundation

catalogue.description: The casing opens and moves to make the processing story easier to follow. Its geometry is a visual design element.
catalogue.title: Processor casing

catalogue.description: These gold pins complete the processor silhouette. They are decorative and do not represent physical interfaces used by the prototype.
catalogue.title: Connection pins

catalogue.description: Seven light arcs rearrange into an orbit, helix, shield and evidence frame. These shapes visually connect the chapters.
catalogue.title: Transforming arcs

catalogue.description: The intersecting rings illustrate how the model considers a sequence of events. They are a visual metaphor for context across ten time steps.
catalogue.title: Context rings

catalogue.description: The red marker introduces unexpected activity at an industrial node. This animation is a demonstration; no attack is sent to a network.
catalogue.title: Illustrative threat
catalogue.visibility: This part appears in the intrusion chapter.

catalogue.description: The wireframe boundary visualizes a proposed containment response. Actions in this portfolio are simulated and do not isolate real devices.
catalogue.title: Containment boundary
catalogue.visibility: This part appears in the response chapter.

explorer.description: Self-attention relates events across the sequence to provide temporal context. The separated plate makes that processing stage visible.
